neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was related to the victim, was involved in an incident where the victim sustained severe facial injuries from an axe, leading to his death. The victim's wife, who was sleeping nearby, witnessed the attack and raised an alarm. The victim was taken to the hospital where he was declared dead. The accused's blood-stained scarf and axe were recovered and tested, showing a match with the victim's blood type. The prosecution's case was corroborated by multiple witnesses and forensic evidence, establishing the accused's involvement in the fatal incident.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused caused severe axe blows on the face of the victim, resulting in his death. The evidence of prosecution witnesses, recovery of blood-stained scarf and axe at the instance of the accused, FSL report, and the evidence of the wife of the deceased corroborated by medical evidence established that the deceased met a homicidal death due to the accused's actions.

quotes.text: From the evidence of prosecution witnesses, recovery of blood stained scarf of accused and blood stained axe at the instance of the accused, the FSL report and the evidence of the wife of deceased corroborated by the medical evidence, it could not be disputed that the deceased had met the homicidal death on account of severe wounds on his face caused by the accused with the axe.

defence_argument.value: The accused denied the charges, asserting his innocence and requesting absolution from the charges. He argued that the name of the accused was not mentioned in the FIR initially due to his wife's priority to take her husband to the hospital for treatment.

quotes.text: The accused denied the charges and submitted that he is innocent and prayed for absolving the charges levelled against him.

To this she has offered an explanation that at that time her uppermost anxiety was to take her injured husband to the hospital for treatment, therefore, the name of the Appellant could not be mentioned in the FIR.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that the evidence of res gestae witnesses, along with corroborative evidence, can establish the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt.

quotes.text: The evidence of the wife of the deceased and other witnesses stands fully corroborated with each other's version - Their evidence is of sterling quality and deserves to be accepted.
Under Section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act'), PW-5 and PW-6 were to be treated as Res Gestae witnesses.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the evidence conclusively established that the accused caused the fatal blow on the deceased, leading to his death, and the courts below had already upheld the conviction and sentence.

quotes.text: From the FSL report and the evidence of P.Ws 2, 3, 5 and 6, it is clearly established beyond shadow of any doubt that the appellant was the person who had caused the fatal blow on the deceased causing his death.
Thus, there is no scope for any interference in the concurrent findings recorded by the two courts below.
